dossier.public_summary: The 3.6-day dip lands exactly on the star's 3.58-day spot cycle and its depth wildly changes from sector to sector and between odd and even dips, with negative depths, all on a very spotted star. This is spot modulation, not a transiting planet.

reasons.why: Signal period 3.56 d equals stellar rotation period 3.581 d, exactly 1.0 multiple, on a VARIABLE K dwarf with rotation amplitude 30313 to 111151 ppm.

Depth changes by factor 252.3% (408 to 1536 ppm) and sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source with p_constant 1.1602591756984554e-69 inside SPOC 2-min, so deep spot-induced dips mimic transits on active sectors.
No transit is consistent: individual depths range from -761 to 2496 ppm with outliers sigma 13.9 and 12.0, chi2 2584.85504944858 dof73, matching spot crossings rather than a stable planet.
Odd 916 ppm vs even 783.9 ppm differ by 132 ppm (ratio 1.2) with sector_oe_max_sigma 8.458 in 3 sectors over 3, expected for evolving spots modulating alternating transits, not a strict binary.
Phase-curve swing 156.6 ppm (ratio_to_depth 0.1763, chi2 370 dof9) and variability_chi2_dof 41.11 shows coherent stellar variation at the dip period.
Centroid places dip on target, ruling out 21 arcsec neighbour that could cause 22.94% eclipse, but on-target spot signal is best explanation versus blend.
